title: Usd Improvements | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive
description:

summary: # Usd Improvements | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone! I have some great updates to share with you about the USD file format. So, let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn. ## What is USD File Format? For those of you who are already turning to me and asking, “Phoebe, what is the USD file format?”—I recommend maybe skipping this video if you're not familiar. The USD file format is currently mainly used in the entertainment and gaming industries. It is utilized when connecting to Unreal, Omniverse, or other large 3D engines and studios. Our goal is to make it easier for you to create your digital assets, extending beyond just production into the digital world. But if you're not ready for that, don’t worry—maybe one day you will be, or maybe you won’t; it's all okay! ## Improvements to USD File Format We now have improvements to our USD file format. Where can you find these updates? 1. **Navigating to USD Layering Option** - First off, go to the settings at the top of the screen. - Open up the new USD layering option. - In the Settings display, go down to Window, and you will find the USD Layer option. 2. **Creating and Managing Layers** - When you open the USD Layer, you will see it on the left side. You can click this to create one layer, create another, and start building layers. - You can export these layers out, which is a really cool update. You can also bring in USD layers, and if you'd like, you can clear everything off and start fresh. ## Exporting USDs Additionally, we have made updates when exporting USDs: - Go to **File > Export USD App** to edit your USD or favorite USDs. - Customize your export settings to include different options, such as obstacles and upcoming grounding features. ## Mesh and Material Management You can check off options that will allow you to see all your textures. The USD format allows for renaming of your meshes, which is a significant update. 1. **Renaming Meshes** - I’m going to go back to my Mac to easily see the test setup. - You can rename your meshes and materials as needed. For those of you who know the appropriate mesh naming conventions, you can apply that here. 2. **Including Simulation Data** - We also have the capability to include your garment simulation data along with fur strand data. However, since I don’t have any fur in my project, I won’t be checking that option. 3. **Setting Up the Up Axis** - Another nice update is the ability to specify your up axis. For example, I set mine to Y, and now I can hit OK to bake and create the whole texture for me. ## Importing USD If I want to bring this in, I can import by saying USD open and selecting the appropriate file. The USD layering automatically pops up, allowing me to use the dropdown to see all my meshes. - When I select a mesh, I can view all the pattern information and simulation data for the fabrics. ## Conclusion There is a lot of information here, and if you’re not familiar with the 3D pipeline or anything beyond this point, it might be overwhelming. I struggled to figure it out too, but it is pretty cool. You can select your patterns and adjust things as needed, making it easier to work in other software like Unreal or Omniverse. I hope you enjoyed the video! If you have any questions, use the comment section down below; someone will get back to you. Don't forget to like and subscribe, and check out our channel for more great videos to learn from. Thanks again so much for watching! Keep having fun and glowing, and I’ll see you in the next one!
